findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never true for spawn-context processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: `self.mp_context.Process` (from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`) returns `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` but is NOT a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The guard `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` added in `_ensure_processes_alive` is therefore always False in production. Before this PR `kill()` was called unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`), the restart counter is bumped and a brand-new process is spawned for the same shards, but the hung original is left running. It leaks (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS times per process index), and if it later unblocks, two processes concurrently run `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` against the same Redis shards and both produce to buffered-segments, causing duplicate segments and racy queue updates. The same broken check at line 346 in `join()` means `terminate()` is never invoked either (pre-existing, but now multiplied by N processes), and the early `break` on deadline at line 341 skips cleanup for the remaining processes entirely. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. There is also no test exercising the restart/kill path to catch this.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard list used as a metric tag value corrupts statsd/Datadog tags
findings.body: `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` is passed as the tag value for `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`. The DogStatsD wire format separates tags with commas (`|#k:v,k2:v2`) and Sentry's Datadog backend does not escape tag values, so with the default `--flusher-processes 1` a single process handles all assigned shards and emits e.g. `shard:0,1,2,...,31`, which the agent parses as tag `shard:0` plus bare tags `1`, `2`, ... This both breaks the intended per-shard breakdown and injects garbage tags with unbounded cardinality (the value changes with every rebalance). Additionally the tag key is inconsistent: `shard` on lines 185/195 but `shards` on line 199. Either emit one metric per shard with an integer tag, or tag with `process_index` and drop the joined list.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched, leaving the flush race unaddressed
findings.body: `test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15, and the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 resolves the attribute on the `time` module at call time, so it does nothing. The comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" is therefore wrong: there is still a race between setting `current_drift.value = 9000` and `step.join()` setting `stopped`, and if the flusher thread observes `stopped` before completing one `flush_segments` round-trip with the new drift, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. `test_flusher.py` avoids this by using `from time import sleep` (bound before the monkeypatch). Either do the same here, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a timeout.

findings.title: submit() now issues N× redundant Redis INFO/ZCARD round-trips, one per flusher buffer
findings.body: `submit()` iterates over `self.buffers` (one `SpansBuffer` per flusher process) calling `record_stored_segments()` (line 270) and `get_memory_info()` (line 301). `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` returns memory usage for every node of the Redis cluster regardless of `assigned_shards`, so with N flusher processes every submitted batch now sends N× the `INFO` commands to every Redis node (and the summed `used`/`available` are both inflated N×; the ratio is unchanged only by coincidence). `record_stored_segments` similarly goes from one pipeline to N pipelines. With `flusher_processes=None` (the factory default) N equals the number of assigned shards, so a consumer with 32 partitions issues 32× the previous Redis control traffic on every batch. Call `get_memory_info()` on a single buffer and either keep the original full-shard buffer for `record_stored_segments` or dedupe the calls.

findings.title: flusher_unhealthy counter is now incremented once per shard per event, inflating existing alerts
findings.body: Previously `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` was incremented once per detected crash/hang. The new code loops over every shard handled by the unhealthy process and increments once per shard, so with the default single flusher process covering all assigned partitions a single crash produces e.g. 32 increments. Any dashboards or alert thresholds based on this counter will see an N× jump unrelated to actual failure rate. Emit once per process (tagged with process index or shard count) instead.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called anywhere; the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. The `if not process: continue` check at line 222 is likewise unreachable since process/thread objects are always truthy. Dead code in the restart path makes the already-subtle lifecycle logic harder to audit; remove it.

findings.title: max_processes=0 silently means 'one per shard' and negative values crash with KeyError
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `--flusher-processes 0` as "use as many processes as shards", which is undocumented (the CLI help only says it is a maximum, default 1) and the opposite of what a user passing 0 likely intends. A negative value (e.g. `--flusher-processes -1`) yields `num_processes = -1`, `range(-1)` creates an empty map, and `i % -1 == 0` makes `self.process_to_shards_map[0]` raise `KeyError` in `__init__` on every partition assignment. Validate the option (`>= 1`) in the click option or constructor.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but processes are capped by max_processes (default 1)
findings.body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` and the CLI default for `--flusher-processes` is 1, so in the default deployment a single process handles all shards round-robin. The docstring also still documents a non-existent `:param topic:` and omits `max_processes`. Misleading documentation on the concurrency model of a component that was just made multiprocess will confuse operators tuning it.
